findings.title: Denial cache blocks newly granted permissions and is never invalidated on allow
findings.body: Check returns Allowed:false immediately when permDenialCache contains the key, before consulting fresh permissions or the DB, and the allowed paths (cached-allow at line 131 and DB-allow after line 146) never delete a denial entry. A denial recorded just before a dashboard/folder is created or a grant is added therefore keeps denying the creator/grantee for the full shortCacheTTL (30s), undermining the stated goal of letting creators access newly created resources. Concurrent requests make it worse: a request that started before a grant can finish afterwards, record a denial, and that denial then overrides another request's fresh allow result because nothing clears it.

findings.title: Denied result from stale folder tree is promoted into a longer-lived denial
findings.body: On a cached-permission miss Check re-queries only permissions from the DB; checkPermission still resolves folder inheritance through buildFolderTree, which serves the 30s-cached folder tree. For a dashboard/folder under a newly created folder, the inherited-permission check can therefore still fail after the DB re-query, and line 154 then stores that failure in permDenialCache for a fresh 30s. The stale-folder denial can thus persist up to roughly a folder-cache TTL plus a denial TTL, so the fix does not reliably let creators reach resources in newly created folders.

findings.title: Denial cache key is ambiguously encoded and omits part of the request identity
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates namespace, userUID, action, name and parent with '_' separators and does not include identity type, group or resource. Grafana UIDs can contain underscores, so distinct tuples such as name='a_b', parent='c' and name='a', parent='b_c' produce the same key, and resources that map to the same action string can also share an entry. A denial cached for one resource can consequently fast-path-deny a different resource for 30s. Use an unambiguous encoding (e.g. length-prefixed or hashed components) and include the resource/group and identity type.

findings.title: Every cache-hit-but-not-allowed Check now performs a full DB permission fetch
findings.body: getUserPermissions and getAnonymousPermissions no longer check permCache, so the getIdentityPermissions call at line 139 always runs the basic-role, team-membership and permission-store queries whenever the cached scope map does not allow the request, even when that scope map was just read fresh from permCache. The only mitigation is the per-(action,name,parent) denial entry, so checks against many distinct resource names (including legitimate UI probing or enumeration of non-existent UIDs) each trigger several DB queries; singleflight only deduplicates concurrent identical keys, not sequential requests.
